newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors seek ex-minister's arrest.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors seek ex-minister's arrest.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Thursday sought arrest warrants for a former cabinet minister and two lawmakers as they probed huge loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co, a prosecution official said.

Home Affairs Minister Kim Woo-suk resigned on Wednesday hours before he was grilled by prosecutors investigating whether Hanbo paid kickbacks to politicians and bankers to secure loans of $5.8 billion.
Kim and of the two lawmakers, Hwang Byung-tai, are close associates of President Kim Young-sam.

The other member of the National Assembly is Kwon Roh-kap, a top aide to opposition leader Kim Dae-jung. Kwon has already admitted taking money from Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo, who is now under arrest.
A senior prosecutor has said the three are under suspicion of taking kickbacks from Hanbo.
